question: In the channelized-intersection example in Figure 2A-3, how far from the nose of the island is the YIELD sign shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Drawing B (Channelized intersection) of Figure 2A-3, the sign mounted on the channelizing island is shown with a "2 ft MIN." dimension from the nose of the island (and 2 ft minimum from the side edge of the island as well). The YIELD sign placed along the channelized right-turn roadway is separately dimensioned with a lateral offset of "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." from the edge of the roadway. This 2-foot island clearance is consistent with MUTCD guidance for signs on raised islands. Guidance (recommended): - "Any signs or signals placed on a raised island in the center of an undivided highway should be installed with a clearance of at least 2 feet from the outer edge of the raised island to the nearest edge of the sign or signal, except as permitted in Section 2A.16." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-3, Drawing B ("Channelized intersection") shows the island-mounted sign dimensioned "2 ft MIN." from the nose of the island and "2 ft MIN." from the island's side, with the roadside YIELD sign dimensioned "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." lateral offset. [Image 4] shows the same Figure 2A-3 in full-page context, including the note that lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. [Image 3] shows related Section 2B.18 text noting that at channelized intersections an additional STOP or YIELD sign may be placed on a channelizing island, but it does not dimension the island clearance. [Image 2] and [Image 5] concern yield lines and crosswalk markings and do not bear on this dimension. Citations: - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Section 8A.06 Guidance §3 (p.989) - Page 121 - Page 93
gold_answer: At least 2 feet from the nose of the island.
